narrative: OMX30 enters Wednesday in a well-established bull market (+9.0% above 200-MA, RSI 75.32) with strong technical momentum (MACD bullish, ADX 61.1, ROC-90 +12.6%). Global headwinds persist—US equity weakness, NASDAQ -0.60%, and negative correlation signal (-0.107%)—but European markets hold firm and commodities rally (gold +1.76%, copper +0.79%), benefiting Swedish industrials and miners. The index sits at +0.9% from its 52-week high; however, elevated RSI and Bollinger Band %B=0.75 flag mean reversion risk. Yields are supportive for banks (VIX -1.16% to 15.28) but not yet a tailwind. Watch for US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET and geopolitical headline risk (Ukraine/Russia tensions) for volatility triggers.
morningBrief: OMX30 opens with bullish technicals but overbought signals demand caution. The index is +3.5% above the 50-MA (3180 level) and testing the upper Bollinger band; support lies at 3085 (lower band). Sector rotation favors Industrials and Mining on commodity strength and strong SEK exporters (USD/SEK +0.44%): Volvo, Atlas Copco, and Boliden are prime beneficiaries. Banks (SEB A, Handelsbanken A) are neutral to mild positive on stable yields (US 10Y at 4.684%). Avoid chasing the rally—RSI 75.32 warns of pullback risk; use any dips toward 3123 (yesterday's close) as better entry points for long positions. Watch for US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET (could reignite rate-cut hopes if weak) and monitor geopolitical headlines. Tech/Telecom (Ericsson, Hexagon) remain pressured by NASDAQ weakness but not severely. Overall bias remains bullish on trend, but exercise discipline on positioning in a toppy market.
